# Grounding Research Digest

*Generated by the prd-grounding-research workflow (run wf_a6d0ad86-e66, 2026-07-15): 4-angle web sweep (comparables, stack patterns, performance, a11y/SEO) synthesized. Feeds prd.md §10 NFRs, §11 Aesthetic, §15 Risk, §8 Open Questions, and addendum.md integration patterns. Preserved here so it survives session end.*

## Positioning

For this audience (recruiters, founders, hiring managers, senior/staff peers) the decisive tension is credibility vs. spectacle, not WebGL vs. content. Substance wins: multiple hiring-manager sources are blunt that "if the most interesting technical thing in your portfolio is the portfolio website itself, you have a problem," and ~80% of recruiters spend under 3 minutes (many decide in 10-30s), frequently on mobile or locked-down corporate machines. The winning move is that the ascent metaphor is DIEGETIC to this specific career — radio waves on the ground (SDR/embedded) → web/Flash/Rails era → clouds (computer vision) → stratosphere (distributed systems) → orbit/deep space (agentic AI). Framed that way, the spectacle IS the resume and IS a live demonstration of the claimed graphics + agentic-AI engineering skill, which closes the "why does an engineer have a game site" gap instead of reading as decoration.

To raise credibility rather than lower it: (1) commit to ONE defended idea (vertical time+altitude ascent) and budget everything around restraint — no shader zoo; the failure mode across every roundup is "every section competes as a hero, nothing breathed." (2) Structure each era as a film beat (entrance / hold / exit) where the calm, readable "hold" state carries recruiter substance, and each era links in seconds to a real deep-dive write-up (architecture, decisions, tradeoffs, measurable impact) plus a live demo or repo — 84% of employers want working applications, not just repos. (3) Ship a genuinely CO-EQUAL HTML "truth" layer: SSR/crawlable, keyboard-navigable, reduced-motion-safe, with a persistent always-visible "skip the experience / see the timeline" control, so an information-seeker gets the full story in under 30 seconds without ever booting WebGL. (4) Publish the source repo + a short build case study — for a technical audience a documented, reproducible, performant build is itself a credibility multiplier, and shipping something janky on a recruiter's mid-tier phone actively destroys the signal. Reference-class solo/agency work (Bruno Simon, The Monolith, Primland, Cartier) proves the concept is buildable; the risk is execution taste, performance discipline, and solo scope — not feasibility.

## Recommended NFR / Budget Targets

### Core Web Vitals (launch gate)
- **Target:** LCP <=2.5s, INP <=200ms (target <100ms), CLS <=0.1 at p75 across BOTH mobile and desktop, measured on field/CrUX data. LCP element must be SSR'd hero/timeline text, never the canvas.
- **Why:** Concrete ranking + UX signal for a heavy WebGL stack; the LCP-is-text rule forces deferring Three.js out of the critical path so an empty canvas never becomes the LCP element.

### Frame budget / FPS floor
- **Target:** 60fps desktop target with a hard <=10ms JS/CPU work ceiling per 16.6ms frame (browser reserves ~6ms). NFR floor: >=45fps on a mid-range 2-3yr-old Android/iPhone under sustained scroll; if average FPS <40 for >2s, auto-downgrade one quality tier.
- **Why:** Recruiters use mid-tier mobile and thermally-throttled/locked-down machines; a set-and-forget quality set at load collapses (60fps can decay to ~20fps after ~30s), so the adaptive loop must react to decline.

### Draw calls
- **Target:** Target <=50 mobile / <=100 desktop per frame; absolute ceiling 1000. Enforce via a renderer.info.render.calls assertion in a perf CI gate.
- **Why:** Draw calls are the single highest-impact metric; degradation is severe above ~500. Requires merging static geometry, sharing materials, and instancing all repeated elements.

### Triangles
- **Target:** <=500,000 total scene triangles; environment props 500-5,000 tris each; sphere/geometry segment counts tuned to camera distance via LOD.
- **Why:** Over-tessellation is a silent mobile killer (50 high-segment spheres can drop a mid-range phone below 30fps); a distance/altitude world must LOD distant waypoints to low-poly.

### Instancing
- **Target:** All stars/particles/repeated era 'nodes' via InstancedMesh/BatchedMesh (target 1 draw call per group). CPU-updated instances <=50,000; use GPU/TSL compute path for higher (WebGPU-gated). Per-tier caps ~ tier3 100k / tier2 30k / tier1 <=10k / tier0 static.
- **Why:** Enables the dense deep-space finale without tanking FPS. Caveat: profile heavy per-instance cases — InstancedMesh can be slower than a merged Mesh, so it is not a blind win.

### Texture memory & format
- **Target:** <=256-384MB GPU texture memory on mobile (stay under iOS Safari's ~300-500MB WebGL heap), <=1GB desktop. All 3D textures KTX2 (ETC1S color / UASTC normal-data), mipmapped, max 1K mobile / 2K desktop; no uncompressed PNG/JPG above ~256px in the 3D layer.
- **Why:** iOS Safari memory is the #1 cause of WebGL tab crashes; KTX2 stays compressed in VRAM (4-8x saving) and uploads 4-8x faster.

### Geometry transfer
- **Target:** All downloaded meshes Draco- or Meshopt-compressed (~80-95% size reduction; Meshopt preferred for web). Count decode cost against the load-time budget, NOT the frame budget.
- **Why:** Compression shrinks transfer only; CPU decode happens before GPU upload — blocking the main thread decoding meshes mid-scroll causes jank, so decode belongs in the initial/progressive-reveal phase.

### Asset weight
- **Target:** First-meaningful WebGL load <6MB (benchmarked vs Awwwards SOTD Messenger's 5.7MB); hard total cap ~15MB; per-era lazy loading so the full world never downloads up front; preload only the adjacent era on scroll approach.
- **Why:** Keeps first paint fast and bounds memory; ties to 'scroll distance = years' where longer eras = more streamed chunks.

### devicePixelRatio
- **Target:** Clamp to min(devicePixelRatio, 2) globally; drop to 1.0-1.5 on low/mid GPU tier and during active scroll/camera-launch via AdaptiveDpr.
- **Why:** Highest-leverage mobile fill-rate saving — phones report DPR up to 3 (~9x the pixels / fragment-shader cost); pairs directly with postprocessing gates.

### Bundle & threading
- **Target:** R3F/Three bundle deferred until AFTER the load event (never in the critical path); shader compile + geometry parse + texture decode moved into a Web Worker via OffscreenCanvas; Three core kept near its ~500KB-1MB tree-shaken floor.
- **Why:** Locks LCP onto text and keeps INP <100ms through load (AthenaHQ pattern); guards against layout shift when the canvas mounts.

### WebGL contexts / canvas topology
- **Target:** Exactly ONE persistent GlobalCanvas fixed behind the scrolling document for the entire site; never mount a per-section or per-era <Canvas>. Switch era scene graphs via the `visible` prop (stay mounted, pre-warm materials); never conditional mount/unmount at runtime.
- **Why:** Browsers cap simultaneous WebGL contexts (~8-16) and kill the oldest (blank sections); conditional mount/unmount recompiles materials/buffers causing hitches exactly at era transitions.

### Scroll authority & RAF loop
- **Target:** GSAP ScrollTrigger on the real (native/Lenis) document is the SINGLE scroll authority — no drei ScrollControls in the same route. One RAF: Lenis autoRaf:false, gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0), drive lenis.raf() from gsap.ticker (remember time*1000 s->ms), ScrollTrigger.update() on Lenis's scroll event.
- **Why:** ScrollControls' overlay div breaks the SEO/semantic truth layer and its easing desyncs pinned/scrubbed camera; two competing RAF loops cause visible DOM<->WebGL jitter.

### State boundary
- **Target:** Per-frame values (camera position, scrollProgress, physics) live in refs or are read via Zustand store.getState() inside useFrame — NEVER setState in useFrame or scroll callbacks. React re-render reserved for discrete UI only (activeEra, qualityTier, reducedMotion).
- **Why:** Routing 60fps updates through React's scheduler is the single most common R3F perf failure (re-render storms/frame drops).

### Camera model
- **Target:** Author the full ground->orbit->deep-space journey as ONE scrubbable timeline; map scrollProgress->timeline position each frame (tl.seek(offset*duration)); reuse the same timeline for click-to-launch by tweening the playhead to a waypoint, not hijacking scroll. If Theatre.js is used, Studio is dev-only (NODE_ENV-guarded, tree-shaken) and animation baked to a checked-in state.json.
- **Why:** Single-timeline design keeps continuous scroll and nonlinear launch consistent and makes both DOM section heights and world waypoints derivable from one shared config (prevents drift).

### Rendering mode & physics
- **Target:** frameloop='demand' + explicit invalidate() during scroll/tween/physics; zero renders when idle; regress() during interaction. Rapier scoped to active-era accent props only, world paused when the era is off-screen, disabled entirely in Low tier / reduced-motion; raycasting throttled to ~30Hz.
- **Why:** Major battery/thermal win and keeps within the 10ms/frame budget; physics is a per-frame CPU cost that otherwise competes with camera smoothness during transitions.

### Postprocessing
- **Target:** Single @react-three/postprocessing EffectComposer (auto-merges passes). Selective bloom via emissive materials + luminanceThreshold~=1, not global bloom. Full stack (bloom/DoF/vignette) tier3/desktop only; bloom at 1/2-1/4 res on tier2; disabled on tier<=1/mobile. DOM legibility must never depend on postprocessing.
- **Why:** Each effect is a full-viewport fragment pass; cost scales with resolution x DPR (~9x on a 3x phone) — the classic 'great on desktop, unusable on mid-range phone' trap.

### Quality tiering
- **Target:** pmndrs/detect-gpu tier (0-3) at boot sets initial DPR/particle/postprocessing budgets; drei PerformanceMonitor drives runtime up/down-grading with hysteresis (shed order: postprocessing -> particle count -> DPR -> LOD). Tier 0, no WebGL2, or webglcontextlost => serve the static DOM timeline.
- **Why:** You cannot detect battery low-power mode via web APIs, so live FPS adaptation plus a boot-time GPU tier is the only robust path; must be built in from the start given the launch-quality bar.

### Rendering backend
- **Target:** WebGL2 required baseline (Three.js/R3F); WebGPU is opt-in, gated on successful navigator.gpu adapter+device acquisition with automatic WebGL2 fallback. Do not ship WebGPU-only compute-particle paths.
- **Why:** Despite ~82% support in 2026, driver/OS/mobile-GPU and float-texture gaps persist (notably iOS); a WebGPU-only path breaks for a meaningful slice of recruiter devices.

### Accessibility conformance
- **Target:** WCAG 2.2 Level AA committed as the launch NFR (2.2.2 Pause/Stop/Hide-A, 2.3.1 Three Flashes-A, 1.1.1 Non-text-A, 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks-A, 2.4.3 Focus Order-A, 2.4.7 Focus Visible-AA, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured-AA); additionally satisfy 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA) via the reduced-motion path.
- **Why:** The product IS scroll-linked motion — exactly the pattern 2.3.3 targets — so the reduced-motion fallback is non-optional even though 2.3.3 is AAA.

### Reduced-motion architecture
- **Target:** Spectacle OFF by default in code; enable only when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches === false. A single Zustand flag gates ALL GSAP tweens, parallax, camera launch, and Rapier motion, read on mount AND re-evaluated on the matchMedia 'change' event. In reduced mode: native/instant scroll (scrollTo behavior 'auto'), era clicks jump instantly, transitions limited to opacity/crossfade, rendering the same static vertical timeline as the no-JS fallback. Additionally ship a persistent, keyboard-reachable in-UI 'Reduce/pause motion' toggle.
- **Why:** ~25% of macOS/iOS users enable Reduce Motion; parallax + camera launch are the highest vestibular-trigger patterns. OS setting alone does NOT satisfy 2.2.2 for auto ambient motion >5s, hence the in-UI control.

### Flash safety (hard gate)
- **Target:** No effect (bloom/strobe/warp/lightning/engine-ignition/launch flash) flashes more than 3x per second at large area or high luminance; verify the launch tween and deep-space effects with PEAT. Applies in full-motion mode too — no exception path.
- **Why:** WCAG 2.3.1 Level A is seizure-safety-critical (photosensitive epilepsy) with legal-liability exposure; it is not gated by reduced-motion.

### Canvas semantics & keyboard model
- **Target:** Canvas is aria-hidden (decorative) OR role='img' + aria-labelledby pointing at visible DOM text. Every meaningful era scene has a text equivalent sourced from the DOM (single source of truth). Skip-link as first tab stop -> <main>; each era is a real focusable <button>/<a> in logical DOM order, activatable by Enter/Space, triggering the same navigation as a click; no positive tabindex; heading hierarchy h1 (name) -> h2 (per era). Never raycast-only selection.
- **Why:** A WebGL canvas is invisible to AT by default; canvas-only era selection makes the core interaction unreachable for keyboard/screen-reader users (fails 2.1.1/2.4.3).

### Focus indicator
- **Target:** Never outline:none. Visible focus ring rendered ABOVE the canvas (z-index/stacking), >=3:1 contrast, works on both bright-cloud and deep-space backdrops (e.g. double-outline/halo, not color-only), and the focused element is never obscured by overlays (2.4.11).
- **Why:** Background luminance changes dramatically along the journey, so a single-treatment focus ring will disappear on one end of the ascent.

### SSR & routing
- **Target:** SSR/SSG every indexable route in Next.js so full resume text + headings + links + JSON-LD exist in the initial HTML before hydration and before the canvas mounts. The WebGL layer is a next/dynamic {ssr:false} 'use client' island mounted post-hydration with a poster/skeleton. History-API real URLs per era (e.g. /journey/computer-vision), each with unique SSR'd <title>/meta/canonical; scroll waypoint restorable from URL. No hash/fragment routing.
- **Why:** AI crawlers (GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot) and the first crawl wave read raw HTML only; hash routes aren't crawlable/shareable and break back/forward + deep links.

### Structured data
- **Target:** SSR'd JSON-LD ProfilePage > mainEntity Person { name (required), image, jobTitle, description, sameAs:[LinkedIn, GitHub, ...], knowsAbout/hasOccupation per era, dateModified }. Must be in static HTML (AI crawlers don't run JS) and mirror the visible DOM 1:1. Validate with Rich Results Test in CI.
- **Why:** Enables Person/ProfilePage rich results and generative-engine visibility; client-injected JSON-LD is invisible to non-JS crawlers.

### Static fallback (one artifact, four jobs)
- **Target:** A complete, usable static vertical timeline with all copy/dates/links/images that works with JavaScript disabled AND when WebGL is unavailable. This same artifact serves: the SEO body, the <noscript> mirror, the reduced-motion mode, and the low-end/mobile/context-lost fallback. Optionally opt into the Sec-CH-Prefers-Reduced-Motion client hint so SSR ships it (and skips the R3F bundle) from the first byte.
- **Why:** One well-built artifact satisfies SEO, accessibility, and device-reality failure modes simultaneously — the cheapest high-leverage deliverable in the project.

### Recruiter-conversion & engineering-CI
- **Target:** Full name + current role + one-line pitch + timeline index readable in <30s without WebGL; a persistent on-screen 'skip experience / view timeline' control; 3-5 signature eras each linking to a deep write-up (architecture, decisions, measurable impact) and a live demo or repo. Check a 3D perf-budget JSON into the repo (max bundle, max textures, max draw calls per route) and fail CI on regression; publish the source repo + build case study.
- **Why:** 84% of employers want working apps; for a technical audience a documented, reproducible, budget-enforced build is itself credibility, and CI prevents silent perf regressions as the scene grows.

## Risk Register (researched)

- **(high)** Style-over-substance perception: if the most impressive technical thing is the site itself, senior interviewers' credibility read DROPS and the spectacle reads as a distraction from a thin resume.
  - *Mitigation:* Make the metaphor diegetic to the real career and frame the build explicitly as a demonstration of the claimed graphics/agentic-AI skill; route from every era to a real deep-dive + live demo/repo in seconds; publish the source repo and a build case study.
- **(high)** Vestibular/motion-sickness and disorientation from scroll-jacking, parallax, and the nonlinear camera 'launch' tween — alienates a subset of recruiters and fails the exact pattern WCAG 2.3.3 targets.
  - *Mitigation:* prefers-reduced-motion must REPLACE (not dampen) the camera ascent with the native-scroll static timeline; launch becomes an instant jump/crossfade; ship a persistent in-UI pause/reduce toggle in addition to honoring the OS setting.
- **(high)** iOS Safari GPU-memory crashes: exceeding the ~300-500MB WebGL heap or hitting WebKit context/texture-not-released-on-resize bugs silently kills the tab.
  - *Mitigation:* Enforce <=256-384MB mobile texture budget with KTX2; dispose() geometries/textures/materials when scrolling past an era; debounce resize and never recreate the context on resize; add a webglcontextlost handler that falls back to the static DOM timeline; test on real iPhones.
- **(high)** Performance failure on the exact devices recruiters use (mid-tier mobile, older/locked-down corporate machines) with thermal throttling collapsing 60fps to ~20fps under sustained scroll.
  - *Mitigation:* detect-gpu boot tier + PerformanceMonitor runtime downgrade with hysteresis; AdaptiveDpr; frameloop='demand'; on-mobile ship the static illustrated timeline when 3D would add >1s perceived delay; enforce all numeric GPU/asset budgets.
- **(high)** SEO/AI-search invisibility: if resume content lives only in the canvas it is uncrawlable by Google's first wave and by non-JS AI crawlers, and unshareable.
  - *Mitigation:* HTML-first SSR/SSG of the full timeline as semantic DOM before the renderer boots; per-era crawlable History-API routes; SSR'd JSON-LD ProfilePage/Person mirroring the DOM; verify via Search Console URL Inspection -> View Tested Page -> HTML.
- **(high)** Photosensitive-epilepsy seizures from flashing in the launch tween or postprocessing (strobe/warp/ignition/bloom flicker) — a safety and legal-liability failure.
  - *Mitigation:* Hard gate: no effect flashes >3x/sec at large area/high luminance; test launch + deep-space effects with PEAT; applies even in full-motion mode (WCAG 2.3.1 Level A, no exception).
- **(high)** Canvas-only (raycast) era selection with no DOM equivalents makes the core journey unreachable for keyboard and screen-reader users (fails 2.1.1/2.4.3).
  - *Mitigation:* 1:1 map every era to a real focusable <button>/<a> in logical DOM order, Enter/Space-activatable, triggering the same navigation as a click; canvas aria-hidden or role=img with aria-labelledby.
- **(high)** No adaptive quality: a scene that runs at 60fps on the builder's machine stutters on recruiters' laptops/integrated GPUs, undermining the credibility the site exists to signal.
  - *Mitigation:* Build quality tiers (High/Med/Low) keyed off detect-gpu + PerformanceMonitor from day one; shed postprocessing -> particles -> DPR -> LOD under sustained decline; regress() during interaction.
- **(high)** Over-scope for a solo builder: 5-6 fully-realized Awwwards-caliber 3D eras is a huge surface that risks never reaching the launch bar or shipping uneven eras that undercut the premium impression.
  - *Mitigation:* Fidelity-tier: reserve full 3D for 2-3 signature bookend eras (ground radio-waves, deep-space agentic AI) and use lighter kinetic-type/particle/wireframe treatments for transitional eras; make eras data/config-driven so adding future eras is not a rewrite.
- **(medium)** Choosing drei ScrollControls (or mixing it with ScrollTrigger pin): its HTML lives in a transformed overlay div (breaks the SEO/semantic truth layer) and its easing desyncs pinned/scrubbed camera into jittery, off-by-frames motion.
  - *Mitigation:* Single scroll authority = GSAP ScrollTrigger on the real native/Lenis document; forbid drei ScrollControls in the primary route.
- **(medium)** Two RAF loops (Lenis auto-raf + R3F frameloop) or setState-in-useFrame cause visible DOM<->WebGL jitter and React re-render storms.
  - *Mitigation:* One ticker: Lenis autoRaf:false, lenis.raf driven from gsap.ticker with lagSmoothing(0) (convert time*1000); keep per-frame values in refs/Zustand getState(), React state only for discrete UI.
- **(medium)** Layout-shift/height drift between the DOM truth layer and the scroll-mapped world (since scroll distance = years lived) makes the camera land mid-transition and can blow CLS.
  - *Mitigation:* Derive both DOM section heights and world waypoint offsets from ONE shared timeline/config; use predictable element heights and reserve the canvas box so CLS <=0.1.
- **(medium)** Loading all era GLTFs up front or conditional mount/unmount of era scenes causes multi-second stalls, memory/GPU thrash, and material-recompile hitches exactly at transitions.
  - *Mitigation:* Chunk one Draco/Meshopt model per era behind a Suspense boundary; preload only the adjacent era; toggle `visible` (keep mounted) and pre-warm materials; drop distant eras to a non-meshed/billboard LOD.
- **(medium)** Scroll fatigue and 'nothing breathed' — mapping years to scroll distance makes long tenures tedious and turns every era into a competing hero.
  - *Mitigation:* Bounded per-era waypoints/'altitude chambers' rather than one 5000vh scroll; film-beat pacing (entrance/hold/exit) with calm readable hold states; camera-mode variety (dolly/arc/orbital tumble); cap the longest-tenure scroll length.
- **(medium)** Metaphor legibility: altitude=era can read as cute/gimmicky if the ascent affordance isn't taught in the first seconds and atmospheric cues don't make 'higher = later/more advanced' obvious.
  - *Mitigation:* Diegetic first-cue in 3-5s (Bruno-Simon-style onboarding); budget per-era atmospheric art direction (fog density, horizon curvature, haze, star field) as first-class, not camera height alone.
- **(medium)** Solo maintenance and aging: immersive sites 'age fast without ongoing evolution' and a bespoke per-era render pipeline is unmaintainable — while the ascent metaphor implicitly promises the site keeps growing.
  - *Mitigation:* Adopt a composable/shared rendering system (reused material/particle/transition modules per era, à la The Monolith) and a data-driven era content model so new career eras are added via config, not code rewrites.
- **(medium)** WebGPU false confidence: shipping WebGPU-only compute-particle paths breaks on iOS/driver gaps despite ~82% headline support.
  - *Mitigation:* WebGL2 as required baseline; WebGPU opt-in only after successful navigator.gpu adapter+device acquisition with automatic WebGL2 fallback; verify with real-device telemetry before enabling compute paths.

## PRD Section Implications

- **Architecture / System Design:** Declare a single scroll authority (GSAP ScrollTrigger on native+Lenis document; no drei ScrollControls), ONE persistent GlobalCanvas fixed behind the scrolling document, Zustand as the state bridge read via getState() in useFrame, and the WebGL layer as a next/dynamic {ssr:false} 'use client' island mounted on top of already-SSR'd DOM. Specify the single-RAF loop topology explicitly (autoRaf:false, one ticker).
- **Information Architecture / Content Model:** Eras are data/config-driven (one config object per era feeding the visible timeline, JSON-LD, screen-reader text, world waypoints, and section heights from a SINGLE source). Model each era as a bounded waypoint/'altitude chamber' with its own crawlable route (/journey/<era>) rather than one continuous 5000vh scroll — bounds asset loading, gives distinct art direction, and gives launch a discrete destination.
- **Performance & NFRs:** State the numeric budgets verbatim: CWV gates (LCP<=2.5s/INP<=200ms/CLS<=0.1 p75), <=10ms/frame JS ceiling with >=45fps mobile floor, <=50/100 draw calls, <=500k triangles, <=256-384MB mobile texture memory, DPR<=2, <6MB first load / ~15MB cap. Require detect-gpu + PerformanceMonitor tiering, frameloop='demand', and a checked-in perf-budget JSON with CI enforcement.
- **Accessibility:** Commit WCAG 2.2 AA (plus 2.3.3 AAA via reduced-motion). Specify reduced-motion as a PRIMARY designed mode (not 'animations off'): static timeline, instant scroll, jump/crossfade launch, single Zustand flag re-evaluated on matchMedia change, plus an in-UI pause toggle. Specify flash safety (PEAT), canvas semantics, skip-link + landmarks + heading hierarchy, keyboard-operable era buttons, and focus rings that survive both bright and dark backdrops.
- **SEO / Discoverability:** SSR/SSG every indexable route before the renderer boots; History-API per-era URLs with unique title/meta/canonical; SSR'd JSON-LD ProfilePage>Person in static HTML (not client-injected) mirroring the DOM 1:1; account for non-JS AI crawlers (GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot). Add a Search Console HTML-render check and Rich Results Test to the launch checklist.
- **Content Strategy / Credibility:** Each of 3-5 signature eras links to a real deep-dive (architecture, decisions, tradeoffs, measurable impact) plus a live demo or repo. Guarantee the name + current role + one-line pitch + timeline index are readable in <30s without WebGL, and keep a persistent 'skip experience / view timeline' control on screen at all times. Frame the build as a skill demonstration and plan to publish the repo + case study.
- **Scope / Phasing (solo-builder guard):** Fidelity-tier the eras: full-realized 3D for 2-3 bookend signature eras (ground radio-waves, deep-space agentic AI), lighter kinetic-type/particle/wireframe treatments for transitional eras. Sequence the static truth layer FIRST (it doubles as SEO/noscript/reduced-motion/low-end fallback), then layer WebGL as progressive enhancement.
- **Interaction & Motion Design:** Structure each era as a film beat (entrance / hold / exit) with calm readable hold states; teach the ascent affordance ('scroll up = up in time and altitude') with a diegetic cue in the first 3-5s; author the whole journey as one scrubbable camera timeline where scrollProgress maps to timeline position and click-to-launch tweens the same playhead. Use camera-mode variety and per-era atmospheric cues to signal altitude.
- **QA / Launch Checklist:** Real mid-tier device testing (not desktop/simulator); PEAT flash test of launch + deep-space effects; Search Console URL Inspection HTML check per route; Rich Results Test in CI; perf-budget CI gate on draw calls/bundle/textures; verify webglcontextlost falls back to the static timeline; verify reduced-motion and no-JS both render the complete story.

## Reference-Class / Prior Art

- **The Monolith Project** — <https://themonolithproject.net>
  - Closest structural analog: a 13-scene scroll narrative on the exact target stack (Three.js + R3F + GSAP + custom shaders + GPU particles) that feels like a short film. Sets the credibility bar for scene-to-scene visual cohesion and, via its Codrops case study, the composable-rendering pattern (shared material/particle/transition systems reused per scene) a solo builder must adopt so 5-6 eras don't become 5-6 bespoke pipelines.
- **Bruno Simon portfolio** — <https://bruno-simon.com>
  - Reference-class SOLO WebGL portfolio (drivable car, physics, fully open-source). Two adoptable lessons: onboarding teaches the interaction in the first 3-5s with no tutorial (the ascent affordance needs a diegetic first-cue), and physics must be legible/purposeful not gratuitous. Publishing the repo is itself a credibility multiplier for a technical audience.
- **Explore Primland** — <https://explore.ownprimland.com>
  - Scroll-driven aerial flythrough with atmospheric fog — proves altitude/scale is conveyed by atmospheric cues (fog, haze, horizon), not camera height alone. Directly validates the ground->orbit ascent's legibility device; budget per-era atmosphere as first-class art direction.
- **Sébastien Lempens** — <https://sebastien-lempens.com>
  - Scroll journey through 3D Paris with dynamic camera-mode shifts (first-person scooter, skydiving). Shows how camera-mode variety keeps a long scroll from feeling monotonous — apply distinct camera behaviors per altitude band (ground dolly, arc into clouds, orbital tumble).
- **Igloo Inc** — <https://igloo.inc>
  - Uses scroll to drive a full journey via structural navigation rather than effect density — reinforces the 'one defended idea, restraint over shader-zoo' principle that protects credibility with a senior audience.
- **Codrops: Cinematic 3D scroll with GSAP + Theatre.js/R3F** — <https://tympanus.net/codrops/2023/02/14/animate-a-camera-fly-through-on-scroll-using-theatre-js-and-react-three-fiber/>
  - The concrete camera-authoring pattern: bind one scrubbable timeline's playhead to normalized scroll (sequence.position = scroll.offset * length), reuse it for click-to-launch, and if using Theatre.js keep Studio dev-only and bake animation to a checked-in state.json. Note: its tutorial omits prefers-reduced-motion — a gap to explicitly close.
- **14islands r3f-scroll-rig** — <https://github.com/14islands/r3f-scroll-rig>
  - Production pattern for mixing WebGL with scrolling HTML using ONE persistent GlobalCanvas across route changes (via useCanvas/UseCanvas tunneling and DOM-proxy tracking), solving the WebGL-context-cap problem — the buy-vs-build reference for the single-canvas architecture.

## Research-Surfaced Open Questions

- Which specific 2-3 eras get full-realized 3D vs. lighter kinetic-type/particle/wireframe treatment? (Concept implies ground radio-waves + deep-space agentic-AI as the 3D bookends — confirm and decide the transitional treatments.)
- Camera authoring workflow for a solo builder: Theatre.js Studio (GUI keyframing, dev-only, baked to state.json) vs. code-authored pure GSAP timeline — which fits the maintenance model better?
- Is a live demo and/or public repo actually available for EACH signature era, or will some eras be narrative-only? (84% of employers want working apps; gaps weaken specific eras.)
- Buy vs. build the canvas/scroll sync: adopt 14islands r3f-scroll-rig or drei <View> for DOM-anchored per-section 3D, or hand-roll a single fixed canvas with scroll-driven camera?
- Exact scroll-distance-to-years scale and a cap on the longest tenure — how do we prevent long jobs from becoming a tedious scroll while still honoring 'longer job = more world'?
